subject: FinBank eval setup & benchmarks — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@finbank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: FinBank eval setup & benchmarks — next steps

Hi Julia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of ask
- Goal: run a targeted quality evaluation of LLM responses on your customer support and internal policy examples to measure hallucination and policy compliance.
- Success criteria: <=5% high-severity hallucinations, precision/recall targets on labeled intents (we can formalize).

Dataset & format
- Preferred format: CSV with columns: id, prompt, expected_response, label, sensitivity_flag (PII).
- We usually ingest a sample of ~1k examples for initial evals and ramp to 5-10k for production benchmarking.
- Attached: finbank-eval-template.csv and our redwood-eval-guide.pdf with examples.

Recommended models to try (shortlist)
- redwood-instruct-medium (fast, lower cost)
- redwood-instruct-large-v2 (best quality baseline)
- redwood-vernac-7b-quant (cost-optimized, evaluate for regression)

Scoring & metrics
- Exact match where appropriate, normalized-token F1 for free text, and a custom weighted severity score for compliance issues.
- We can run a human-in-the-loop sampling for edge cases and surface regression alerts.

Sandbox & infra
- We can run the evals on Hosted Redwood for speed, or Dedicated pools if you need isolation. For initial evals Hosted is easiest.

Proposed next steps
1) You confirm dataset sample & redaction plan (PII handling).
2) We run a 1k trial and share benchmark results + prompt set recommendations in 72 hours after ingestion.
3) Optional: join a 60-min kickoff to walk through dataset formatting and scoring.

Please confirm whether the CSV template works and share a sample file (redacted) when ready. I’ll book a kickoff slot next week unless you prefer a different cadence.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134
From: Julia Park <julia.park@finbank.com>

Cc: Ahmed Khan <akhan@finbank.com>, FinBank Consulting <devops@finbank-consulting.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinBank eval setup & benchmarks — next steps

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Attaching a small sample (finbank_sample.csv) — we redacted direct PII but left the sensitivity_flag column for your pipeline. A few answers inline:

- Sample size: we'll start with ~1.2k rows from support transcripts + 200 policy QA items.
- PII: security will require redaction; we can also provide a hashed_customer_id column if needed.
- Scoring: the compliance team prefers a weighted severity score like you suggested (Severity: high/med/low).
- Latency: we are sensitive to tail latency; if redwood-instruct-large-v2 has >300ms tail we might need to consider trimming context or using a smaller model.

Can you confirm sandbox access (temporary creds) and whether you need firewall VPN for any non-hosted runs? Also please share the HubSpot/Drive links for uploads.

Attaching: finbank_sample.csv

Julia Park
Director, Customer Experience | FinBank
julia.park@finbank.com | +1 (212) 555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@finbank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinBank eval setup & benchmarks — next steps

Appreciate the sample, Julia — looks good and the sensitivity_flag is perfect. Quick plan for execution: 

1) Ingest: we’ll use the CSV template and run a validation pass (schema + sampling) within 24 hours of upload.
2) Eval run: initial 1.2k eval across redwood-instruct-medium and redwood-instruct-large-v2 (Hosted) — expected turnaround 72 hours.
3) Metrics & prompts: we’ll produce a report with exact-match/F1 and a compliance severity breakdown, plus a recommended prompt set and mitigation strategies for hallucinations.
4) Follow-up: 45-60 minute results review where we’ll walk the scoring, show example failures, and recommend rollout options (caching, quantized models, or Dedicated if you need isolation).

For sandbox access: we’ll send temporary API keys scoped to an eval-only project and a short guide for uploading to a secure Drive link. No VPN required for Hosted evals; Dedicated/VPC runs would be different and we can cover that in the kickoff.

I’ve created a HubSpot deal and uploaded a mutual action plan — links below. If that timeline works I’ll set the kickoff for Thu 4/15 at 10am PT.

Subject: RE: FinBank eval setup & benchmarks — next steps

Internal notes for the run: 
- Start models: redwood-instruct-medium (baseline), redwood-instruct-large-v2 (quality baseline). If latency becomes an issue, fall back to redwood-vernac-7b-quant for cost/latency tradeoff.
- Prompt sets: include a) support Q/A canonical prompts, b) policy interpretation prompts, c) higher-risk multi-step prompts to catch chain-of-thought hallucination.
- Scoring: implement token-normalized F1 + a heuristics-based compliance tagger (simple regex + LLM re-check) for high/med severity.
- Run config: 1k initial; use stratified sampling across channels and severity.

I’ll prep the eval job template and the ingestion checklist (schema validation + PII confirmation). Neha, can you own the MOP for the upload and the API key provisioning?

-Vivek
